title: Saving water every day
description: Shorter showers, fixed drips, and full loads: easy water habits that also trim bills.

body.heading: The drip maths
paragraphs: A dripping tap can waste litres of water every day, and a running toilet can waste far more without making a sound. Fixing drips promptly is one of the cheapest resource saves there is.
If you are unsure whether a toilet is leaking, your water provider's website usually explains simple checks you can do at home.

body.heading: Daily habits that stick
paragraphs: Shorter showers, turning the tap off while brushing teeth, and running washing machines and dishwashers only when full all save water without any sense of sacrifice.
Heating water takes energy, so saving hot water saves twice: once on the water bill and once on the energy bill.

body.heading: Outside counts too
paragraphs: Water gardens in the cooler parts of the day so less evaporates, and let lawns go a little golden in dry spells — they usually recover when rain returns.

takeaway: Fix drips fast, save hot water where you can, and run machines only when full.
